title: Practice: frequency polygons
intro: Eight questions on plotting and reading frequency polygons.

questions.prompt: Emma describes how to draw a frequency polygon. Select **every** correct statement.

options.text: Plot each point at the midpoint of its class
Plot each point at the start of its class
The height of each point is the frequency
Join the points with a smooth curve
Join the points with straight lines

hints: Which value represents the whole class?
questions.explanation: Midpoints, at the height of the frequency, joined with straight lines.

questions.prompt: Insect larvae lengths. Complete the points you would plot.
Horses sold at a market: $350$–$400$ kg: 16, $400$–$450$: 130, $450$–$500$: 42, $500$–$550$: 12. Set the polygon to match. (The slider maximum is 140.)
hints: Set each class's slider to its frequency.

questions.prompt: What is the mid-interval value of the class $500 \le m < 550$?
Students' travel times peak at $15$–$20$ minutes; teachers' at $10$–$15$ minutes. Which conclusion is best?

options.text: Teachers generally take less time to travel to school
Every teacher is faster than every student
The two groups take the same time

hints: A peak shows where most of the data is, not every value.
questions.explanation: The teachers' polygon is shifted to the left, so teachers **generally** take less time. It says nothing certain about every individual or about where people live.

questions.prompt: You should join the last point of a frequency polygon back to the first to close the shape.
hints: Despite the name, it is not a closed polygon here.
questions.explanation: False. Join neighbouring points only, from the first class to the last.

questions.prompt: A frequency polygon of 40 cars' prices has points at $(1750, 4)$, $(2250, 14)$, $(2750, 13)$, $(3250, 4)$ and one more at $3750$. What is the frequency at $3750$?
hints: The frequencies must add up to 40.
